content.text: Let me validate the JSON parses and run the storage test.

Both fixes are in. Here's what was wrong.

## What was broken

The project had **two independent bugs**, either of which alone would produce a blank map:

### 1. The layer was never connected to the renderer (the main bug)
The `/scatterplot-layer` node existed and was fully wired up (data, position, radius, color), but its output was never connected to the `DeckRendererOp`'s `layers` input. The renderer had no layers to draw, so nothing appeared.

The edge list had connections *feeding into* the scatterplot layer, but no `/scatterplot-layer.out.layer → /deck.par.layers` edge. I added it:
```json
{
  "id": "/scatterplot-layer.out.layer->/deck.par.layers",
  "source": "/scatterplot-layer",
  "target": "/deck",
  "sourceHandle": "out.layer",
  "targetHandle": "par.layers"
}
```

### 2. Wrong column casing in the position accessor
The `/position-accessor` used `[d.longitude, d.latitude]` (lowercase), but the CSV columns are `Longitude` and `Latitude` (capitalized). `FileOp` parses CSV with `d3.autoType`, which preserves the original header casing — so `d.longitude` was `undefined`, and every point would have gotten position `[undefined, undefined]` even once the layer was connected. Fixed to `[d.Longitude, d.Latitude]`.

(The magnitude accessor already correctly used `d.Magnitude`, which is why the color/radius pipeline was fine — only the position accessor had the casing mistake.)

I confirmed the fixes against the sibling `california-earthquakes` example, which is the correct/working version of this same graph — it has both the `layers` edge and the capitalized `[d.Longitude, d.Latitude]` accessor. The JSON still parses cleanly. Load `/examples/quake-map-broken` in the browser to visually verify the earthquake points now render over California.
